interpretation: Exact historical earnings-date proximity retains substantially more MI than a point-in-time-safe fixed-cycle approximation. This does not prove contamination, but the signal cannot be treated as production-safe alpha without archived schedule snapshots.

exact_contract.definition: next final-observed yfinance earnings date minus cutoff
exact_contract.reason: historical dates are final observed event dates rather than archived point-in-time schedule snapshots

rough_contract.definition: last confirmed actual earnings date available by cutoff + fixed 90 calendar days

cross_ticker_behavior.AAP: Rough 3-day and 5-day windows reverse the exact positive lift; fixed-cycle proximity is not stable.
cross_ticker_behavior.POWI: Rough proximity remains positive but weaker than exact-date proximity.
cross_ticker_behavior.conclusion: The rough signal is largely POWI-driven and does not reproduce the prior two-ticker common signal.

cycle_sensitivity.note: The significant 95-day windows are POWI-driven while AAP MI remains near zero, so this is not cross-ticker robustness.

safe_first_feature_contract.name: earnings_schedule_uncertain_blackout
safe_first_feature_contract.definition: 1 when days since the last confirmed actual earnings event is between 70 and 110 calendar days; otherwise 0
safe_first_feature_contract.production_backtest_rule: Do not use yfinance final historical future earnings dates as known-at-time features.
safe_first_feature_contract.live_rule: A current announced date may only be used after storing a timestamped schedule snapshot; subsequent reschedules must remain auditable.

next_required_work: begin timestamped daily earnings-calendar snapshot accumulation
design a point-in-time schedule change log
test blackout impact on trade risk rather than treat exact proximity as alpha
keep historical estimate revision features deferred
